title: `Alt + Right Arrow` Unexpectedly opens a floating pane on macOS in Zellij v0.41.1
body:
## Issue description
As of Zellij v0.41.1, pressing `Alt + Right Arrow` (`Option + Right Arrow` on macOS) unexpectedly opens a new floating pane. I attempted to unbind this key (unbind "Alt Right"), but the issue persists. Based on WezTerm sends the sequence `\x1bf` when `Alt + Right Arrow` is pressed. The issue occurs even with Zellij’s default configuration.

## Environment
MacOS 14.7.1
WezTerm 20240203-110809-5046fc22
Zellij v0.41.1
Fish 3.7.1

## Minimal reproduction
1. Open zellij (on macOS)
2. Press `Alt` (`Option` key ⌥ on mac) + `right arrow`
3. See new floating pane being opened

## Other relevant information
- Unable to test on other operating systems to determine if this is macOS-specific.
- This behavior was also confirmed using macOS’s built-in Terminal app and zsh, so it seems it's not related to terminal emulator or shell.

For me setting `enable_kitty_keyboard = true` in wezterm configuration doesn't fix it 😔

Edit: Removing this from my wezterm configuration actually fixes the issue:
```lua
{ key = "RightArrow", mods = "ALT", action = wezterm.action.SendString '\x1bf' }
```

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
Taking a cue from @reporter's commants, I ran cat and checked the signals from the left and right arrow keys.
left: `^[[D`, right: `^[[C`
But if we type the arrow keys like Alt, it looks like this
left: `^[b`, right: `^[f`

Meanwhile, on my alt-enabled iTerm2, this is not happening, and when I checked the arrow key signaling, if I press alt and type arrow keys, no arrow key input occurs.
~~Maybe it's a dumb idea... but considering the floating pane default shortcut is `Alt + F`, I wonder if it's caused by parsing the `ESC + F` sequence incorrectly?~~

comments.author: participant3
comments.body:
And... if I change the toggle floating pane shortcut `Alt + f` to `Alt + x` in `~/.config/zellij/config.kdl`
the issue of opening the floating pane with `Alt + ArrowRight` disappears.

On the other hand, this does not happen with `ESC + f`. If I run cat and press `ESC + F`, it looks like this
ESC: `^[`, f: `f`
So it looks like ESC causes the key to be typed twice, and is treated differently than `Alt + f` or `Alt + ArrowRight`, where `^[f` is typed once.
In a terminal app where `Alt + f` and `Alt + ArrowRight` are the same escape sequence, there doesn't seem to be a way for Zellij to distinguish between the two.

I haven't confirmed this myself, but according to this [reddit](https://<redacted-host>/r/zellij/comments/1gq33xs/in_0411_alt_right_arrow_now_opens_a_new_floating/), it doesn't happen in 0.40.1.

I ended up changing the shortcut to open the floating pan.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Interesting 🤔 For me signals are different:
- Opt + left: `^[[1;3D`
- Opt + right: `^[[1;3C`

Anyways the problem has disappeared for me (with [configuration changes](https://github.com/zellij-org/zellij/issues/3819#issuecomment-2514351608)) so I'll close this issue

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
In Ghostty on Mac, this worked for me:

In `~/.config/ghostty/config`, add:
```
keybind = alt+left=unbind
keybind = alt+right=unbind
```

In `~/.inputrc`, add:
```
"\e[1;3C": forward-word
"\e[1;3D": backward-word
```

The `~/.inputrc` change isn't needed for the fish shell or zellij (the ghostty unbinds were enough), but the inputrc does help renable alt+left and alt+right in bash.

The helix editor was also affected by the unbind, but I like the result better (alt+left/alt+right now select whole blocks, which is more powerful than simple cursor navigation).
